item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: The night sky: Moon and calendars
item.stem: Meera's teacher asks why solar calendars add a leap day about every four years. Which statement is correct?

options.A: A leap day is added because the Moon takes exactly 28 days to orbit the Earth.
options.B: Earth takes nearly 365.25 days to revolve around the Sun, so the extra quarter-days add up to about one full day every four years, and the leap day keeps the calendar aligned with the seasons.
options.C: Calendars have 365 days by rule, and leap years are just arbitrary extra days chosen by governments.
options.D: A leap day is added to correct the time Earth takes to spin once on its axis.
